title: 2028-07-18 Verdant AI POC traffic & benchmark scoping
summary: Discovery/POC scoping to define traffic profile, success metrics, benchmark plan and timelines for a 4-week Verdant AI pilot. Key asks: sample traffic (1 week), golden prompt set, SLA targets (95th/99th latency), budget constraints and integration notes for VPC/KMS. Agreed next steps: share benchmark template, schedule traffic replay step, Redwood to propose bench environment and run initial micro-bench within 5 business days.

meeting_header:
Date: 2028-07-18 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Ana Gomez (Redwood CSM), Alex Chen (Verdant Eng Lead), Maya Rao (Verdant Head Infra), Tom Bishop (Verdant CTO), Rina Patel (Verdant ML)
Recording: fireflies.ai transcript export
Meeting notes: POC scoping for traffic modeling, benchmarks, success criteria and timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna go through the POC plan and traffic profile. Quick round robin, please state name and role.
[00:06] Alex: Alex Chen, engineering lead at Verdant.
[00:08] Maya: Maya Rao, infra, hi.
[00:10] Tom: Tom Bishop, CTO.
[00:12] Rina: Rina Patel, ML.
[00:14] Jordan: Jordan Mills, AE Redwood. Priya and Liam from my team will cover bench details.
[00:20] Priya: Hi all, quick agenda: confirm success criteria, walk through current traffic shape (QPS, concurrency), sample token distributions, then benchmark plan and timeline.
[00:28] Jordan: Alex, can you start with current prod profile? Rough numbers are fine.
[00:33] Alex: Yeah, numbers are estimates. Peak QPS about 180 reqs/sec across north america, sustained average like 45 QPS. Concurrency per model call varies — typically 30 to 60 active connections during peaks, but bursts up to 250 for short windows when campaigns run.
[00:49] Rina: Response lengths vary a lot. For our summarization pipeline input tokens average 320, output about 60; for chat assistant flow input 120, output 240 — so two modes. Token mix skews to short outputs overall but tail matters.
[01:05] Maya: We have a hard budget cap for hosted inference, so cost per 1M tokens matters. We're considering Redwood Dedicated vs hosted but security reqs push us to VPC/private later.
[01:17] Priya: OK those numbers help. For the POC we usually ask for at least one week of traffic to model diurnal and burst behavior, plus a golden prompt set for qualitative checks. Can you provide that?
[01:28] Alex: Yep we can do 7 days anonymized. We will need guidance on masking PII — Rina will own that.
[01:34] Tom: Our success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 180ms for short completions (<=64 output tokens), 99th < 500ms; throughput to keep total cost within X (we gave a rough budget in the RFP). Also quality regressions <= 2% on our eval set.
[01:51] Jordan: Good concrete targets. We'll map those to instance types and concurrency profiles. Quick Q: are you using KV cache or any prefix caching today?
[01:58] Alex: We do some in-memory prefix caching in our app tier but not KV cache at model layer.
[02:03] Priya: Great, Redwood has prefix/KV cache options that dramatically reduce repeated-token costs for chat flows. We'll include a caching profile in the bench config.
[02:12] Rina: For benchmarks we want synthetic replay and a live pass. Synthetic replay can reproduce QPS shape precisely, but live pass checks end-to-end network and infra interactions.
[02:22] Liam: We typically run three phases: micro-bench (single instance, multiple concurrency points), replay bench (traffic replay at scale), and golden prompt quality validation. Micro-bench gives us per-GPU token/sec and tail latency.
[02:33] Maya: Which GPU types do you suggest? Our infra team prefers A100 80GB equivalents, but if Redwood has optimizations on certain quantized configs we can try cheaper options.
[02:44] Priya: We'll recommend candidate configs: unquantized on A100 for baseline, int8/awq on T4-like or smaller for cost experiments, and a quantized int4 path if model supports. We'll specify kernels and batch size per sequence length.
[02:58] Alex: Important: our model is a trimmed open-architecture 7B variant with a custom tokenizer — small vocab differences cause token counts to shift. Can you handle that?
[03:08] Priya: Yes, we ingest your tokenizer and compute tokens during replay. Slight mismatches show up in token distribution numbers; we'll report tokenization deltas.
[03:15] Tom: On security, SOC2 is fine, but we need KMS integration for Dedicated/Private and audit logs retention for 12 months. Any blockers?
[03:24] Jordan: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit forwarding. For Dedicated we can enable KMS with limited key access; we'll share the security pack.
[03:31] Maya: Also SSO/SAML for our team, RBAC so only the bench agents can run experiments.
[03:36] Ana: We'll attach the SSO guide and roles mapping.
[03:39] Jordan: Let's walk through benchmark success gates. Phase 1: micro-bench must show per-GPU throughput consistent with modeled expectations. Phase 2: replay bench should demonstrate sustained QPS at up to 120% of your projected peak with 95th/99th under SLAs. Phase 3: quality check — golden prompts must be within your regression threshold.
[03:58] Alex: If we fail phase 2 due to tail latency, what does Redwood do? Autoscale? Fallback to cheaper model?
[04:06] Priya: We can test routing policies: pre-warming, burst autoscaling, fallback to smaller model or degraded quality mode. The POC will include an experiment toggling fallback policies to measure impact on latency and cost.
[04:18] Rina: How do we measure cost parity? We need per-token cost estimates including batching and KV cache effects.
[04:25] Liam: Bench outputs include per-token CPU/GPU ops, batching multiplier, cache hit rate assumptions and modeled cost per 1M input/output tokens. We'll provide a cost breakdown template.
[04:35] Tom: Timeline? We need results before our architecture review on Aug 15. That gives about 4 weeks.
[04:42] Jordan: That's doable. Proposed timeline: week 0 (this week) prep and data upload, week 1 micro-bench and config tuning, week 2 replay bench, week 3 quality eval and follow-ups, week 4 final report and cost model.
[04:56] Maya: Does the replay bench need long-running warm-up to populate KV cache?
[05:01] Priya: Yes. We'll run a warm-up pass (24-48 hours depending on traffic shape) or synthetic warm-up to mimic history. If you can provide historical sessions, we can reproduce warm start conditions.
[05:12] Alex: We have session logs for 30 days; we'll select a subset. Need guidance on anonymization.
[05:18] Rina: We'll remove PII, hash IDs and remove IPs.
[05:21] Jordan: Good. For the replay harness we will need: traffic in JSONL with timestamps, request payloads, and response length targets. We can take either raw requests or condensed event tuples.
[05:31] Alex: We can do JSONL.
[05:33] Priya: On measurement: for latency we'll emit client-side and server-side timestamps to separate network vs infra latency. Provide your sidecar timing if possible.
[05:43] Maya: We'll add sidecar timestamps from our ingress LB.
[05:46] Tom: On KPIs, besides latency and cost, we care about error rate (5xx), model degradation and tail P99.9 — please include p99.9 in the report.
[05:58] Priya: Will do. Also we'll include token distribution histograms (input len, output len), concurrency heatmap by hour, and burst shape quantiles.
[06:09] Rina: For quality evals, we need to run our golden prompts and then a human spot-check at 100 samples. Do you support human-in-the-loop evaluation or do we need to bring our own raters?
[06:20] Liam: Redwood can run the automated eval and provide diff metrics; human rating is customer-provided, but we can integrate with a Mechanical Turk-like flow or your vendor if you want.
[06:29] Alex: We'll bring our raters.
[06:31] Jordan: Anything on SLO windows — do you use 1-min or 5-min windows for percentiles?
[06:36] Tom: We prefer 1-min for detecting microbursts but 5-min for reporting; include both.
[06:41] Priya: Noted. We'll report 1-min and rolling 5-min percentiles and include heatmaps.
[06:47] Maya: One risk — our model uses large KV lookups for retrieval augmented generation; we need to measure KV latency separately. Can you instrument that?
[06:55] Priya: Yes we can instrument KV read latency and include it in the end-to-end trace. If KV is remote we will simulate backpressure.
[07:03] Alex: Any restrictions on uploading sample model weights or tokenizers?
[07:07] Jordan: We usually ask for a pointer to S3 private bucket or ephemeral share link. Avoid sending weights in chat — use secure transfer. We'll sign an NDA if needed but from what I read you already have one in place.
[07:17] Tom: NDA is in place. We'll provision an S3 path and a small role for Redwood bench runners.
[07:23] Rina: For the micro-bench, what concurrency points should we hit to map latency curves?
[07:29] Priya: We'll run concurrency sweeps at 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 for a single instance and then multi-instance scaling. For large models we might increase density.
[07:40] Alex: That should show knee points for batching.
[07:42] Liam: And we'll capture token-level timing, e.g., per-token latency distribution for first 64 tokens vs rest.
[07:49] Jordan: Are there any compliance blockers for us running bench in your VPC?
[07:53] Maya: We prefer Redwood to run in Dedicated within our VPC, but if that's hard, a private peering to Redwood Private is acceptable.
[08:01] Ana: I'll add our private deployment checklist to the repo.
[08:04] Tom: What about fallback policies — will you simulate a smaller but faster model for overflow?
[08:09] Priya: Yes we'll include a fallback run using a 3B variant to measure quality vs cost vs latency trade-offs.
[08:16] Rina: For monitoring, which traces do you need us to ship?
[08:20] Liam: Request ID, client-side timestamp, server-side recv and send timestamps, token counts, model name, instance id, and any KV hit/miss flag. We'll give a JSON schema.
[08:29] Alex: Great.
[08:31] Jordan: Quick recap — deliverables: bench template, config, cost model, micro-bench results, replay bench results, quality report and final recommendations. Timeline aligns to get final report by Aug 15. Any blockers?
[08:43] Tom: No blockers; main items are data upload and infra notes.
[08:47] Maya: We'll prepare anonymized traffic and SSO details.
[08:49] Jordan: Thanks. One last item — if we observe significant tokenization delta that materially changes token counts, we'll surface modeling adjustments and re-run cost calc.
[08:58] Rina: Good.
[09:00] Jordan: Alright I'll send the template after this call. Thanks everyone, we will follow up with invites for the bench planning session.
[09:10] Alex: Thanks all.
[09:12] (meeting ends)
